history.summary: IDENTITY UNVERIFIED: no temple named 'Gadiara Temple' could be identified in Gadiara, Howrah, after multiple web searches, and the geocoder holds no such POI. Gadiara is known as a riverside picnic spot at the Hooghly-Rupnarayan confluence, whose attractions are Fort Mornington (built by Robert Clive after the 1757 Plassey victory to guard against river pirates; ruined in the 1942 flood), an old lighthouse, a West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation tourist lodge, the Ramkrishna Mission Ashrama, and the Mahaprabhu Temple at nearby Pichhaldaha village - none of which matches this CSV name. This entry therefore documents the Gadiara locality itself; coordinates are the town's (ferry ghat area, Shyampur-I, PIN 711314). name: Gadiara Temple
town_description: Gadiara is a riverside town in Shyampur block, Howrah district, at the confluence of the Hooghly and Rupnarayan rivers (the Damodar joins nearby) before they flow on to the sea. A British-era fort (Fort Mornington, built by Robert Clive after Plassey in 1757 against river pirates) stands in ruins here after the 1942 flood; there is also an old lighthouse and a state tourist lodge. About 80-85 km from Kolkata, it is a popular picnic and day-trip spot, with a ferry across the river to Geonkhali in Purba Medinipur.
